persona_summary: BA Sophomore, Strategic Management, Tech Entrepreneurship minor, 31 courses, Good standing
question: I'm interested in taking a data analytics course from the IS department to strengthen my Tech Entrepreneurship minor. Can I just sign up?
false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: IS department courses often have IS-specific prerequisites (e.g., an intro IS course or specific programming course) that BA students haven't taken. The student assumes cross-department enrollment is straightforward, but prerequisite barriers may exist. Additionally, some courses may be restricted to IS majors.
naive_system_response: A naive system might check if the course is offered and confirm availability without checking whether BA students can take IS courses or whether IS-specific prerequisites are satisfied.
correct_response: The data analytics course [XX-XXX] has prerequisites: [specific IS courses]. As a BA student, you likely haven't taken [prerequisite course]. Additionally, check whether this course has a major restriction — some IS courses are reserved for IS students or require department permission. You would need to: (1) complete the prerequisite first, and (2) confirm enrollment eligibility for non-IS students.
why_multi_agent_helps: The Courses Agent checks prerequisites. The Policy Agent checks enrollment restrictions by major. Together they catch both the prereq gap and the potential major restriction — a single agent might check one but not the other.
key_facts: IS courses may have IS-specific prerequisites BA students lack
Some courses have major/department enrollment restrictions
Cross-department enrollment often has hidden barriers
known_traps: Confirming a course exists without checking prerequisites for this specific student's background
Not checking major-restriction policies on the course
Assuming cross-department enrollment works the same as within-department
advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) which data analytics courses exist in IS department, (2) their prerequisites, (3) whether P-024 has those prereqs, (4) any major restriction policies
